# Mahānidāna Sutta (DN 15 (PTS DN ii 55))

**ID:** DN 15 (PTS DN ii 55)  
**Section:** Dīghanikāya (dn)  
**Collection:** Sutta  
**Title (Pali):** Mahānidāna Sutta  
**PTS:** DN ii 55  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0102m.mul1.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0102m.mul1.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Mahānidāna Sutta* ("The Great Discourse on Causation", DN 15) is the fifteenth sutta of the *Dīghanikāya* and the longest, most comprehensive discourse on dependent arising (*paṭiccasamuppāda*) in the collection [Bodhi 1984; Bodhi 1995]. The narrative opens when Venerable Ānanda approaches the Buddha and remarks that the teaching of dependent origination appears simple and clear; the Buddha firmly rejects this assertion, warning that the doctrine is profound and deep, and proceeds to give a detailed exposition of conditional links [Bodhi 1984]. Notably, instead of the standard twelve-link sequence, the discourse presents a nine-link formulation that omits the first two links (ignorance and volitional formations) and sets forth a reciprocal conditioning relationship between consciousness (*viññāṇa*) and name-and-form (*nāmarūpa*) [Emmanuel 2013; Anālayo 2018; Meisig 2010]. The sutta also includes analyses of feeling (*vedanā*)—stressing that pleasant, painful, and neutral feelings do not coexist—and describes the seven stations of beings/consciousness in the context of rebirth and release [Jantrasrisalai 2008; Anālayo 2014; Anālayo 2018].

**Parallels and text reuse**

- Full parallels: DA 13 大緣方便; MA 97 大因; SHT Sutta 23; T 14 人本欲生; T 52 大生義
- Passage-level parallels: AN 8.66 Vimokkhasutta; DN 16 (PTS DN ii 72) Mahāparinibbāna Sutta; T 1536.9 八法品; MN 77 (PTS MN ii 1) Mahāsakuludāyi Sutta; DN 34 (PTS DN iii 272) Dasuttara Sutta; DN 33 (PTS DN iii 207) Saṅgīti Sutta; AN 9.23 Taṇhāmūlakasutta
- Resembling parallels: AN 8.120; an1.447-454; MN 137 (PTS MN iii 215) Saḷāyatanavibhaṅga Sutta; SF 138; SF 240

**Sources**

- [Bodhi 1984] Bhikkhu Bodhi, The Great Discourse on Causation: The Mahānidāna Sutta and its Commentarial Exegesis (1984) — Setting with Ānanda, place as 15th sutta of DN, and status as longest sutta on causation.
- [Bodhi 1995] Bhikkhu Bodhi, The Great Discourse on Causation: The Mahānidāna Sutta and its Commentaries (1995) — Characterization of the sutta's scope and its commentarial translations.
- [Bodhi 2003] Bhikkhu Bodhi, The Connected Discourses of the Buddha (2003) — Comparison with SN 12:60 sharing the opening narrative.
- [Emmanuel 2013] Steven M. Emmanuel, ed., A Companion to Buddhist Philosophy (2013) — Structure of the causal chain missing the first two standard links, and modern translations.
- [Jantrasrisalai 2008] Chanida Jantrasrisalai, Early Buddhist Dhammakaya (2008) — Content regarding the seven sorts of beings at DN ii 68.
- [Anālayo 2014] Bhikkhu Anālayo, Perspectives on Satipaṭṭhāna (2014) — Analysis of the non-coexistence of the three feelings in DN 15 and parallels.
- [Anālayo 2018] Bhikkhu Anālayo, Rebirth in Early Buddhism and Current Research (2018) — Reciprocal relation of consciousness and name-and-form, parallels, and paritta use.
- [Meisig 2010] Konrad Meisig, ed. (chapter by Roderick S. Bucknell), Translating Buddhist Chinese (2010) — Nine-link formula and four Chinese parallels (including MĀ 97).
